title: A New Light-Powered Material Makes Hydrogen From Water
summary:
Chemists at Oregon State University found a new way to make hydrogen from water using light. Kyriakos Stylianou led the work. His team built a material called a photocatalyst. It can produce hydrogen quickly and efficiently.

Hydrogen is used in fuel cells for vehicles. It is also used to make ammonia, refine metals and manufacture plastics.

A catalyst speeds up a chemical reaction without being permanently changed. A photocatalyst is switched on by light. After it absorbs light, it can use that energy to drive reactions faster.

The material is called BVR-19. It has an unusual sulfur-to-sulfur bond that briefly breaks in light. Stylianou said it does not need an extra expensive metal catalyst. It also forms on its own in water at room temperature.

Most hydrogen today is made from natural gas, which releases carbon dioxide. It costs about $1.50 per kilogram, while "green" hydrogen costs roughly $5 per kilogram. Stylianou said the work gives new design rules that could help lower the cost of green hydrogen.
why_it_matters: Cheaper green hydrogen could help reduce the greenhouse gases that come from making hydrogen the usual way.
